app.title: Assay Analyzer
app.summary: The person first sets each assay's method in Settings: the calibration standard, wavelength, titrant strength, how much repeats may vary, and an optional reference sample or target range to compare against. On each assay's page they download a data-entry template, then upload a CSV or Excel file or type readings into an editable table. The app turns the readings into results by fitting a standard curve, applying a titration or weighing formula, or fitting a dose-response curve, and summarises the repeats with statistics. It shows warnings about data quality, comparison flags and charts, and every assay can be exported to one Excel report. A second path takes results that were already calculated and runs the same summaries and checks on them.

task.text: Turn raw bench readings from several laboratory assays into per-sample results with repeat statistics, quality warnings and reference checks, and export them as an auditable report.

data.text: Long-format tables of bench measurements, one row per reading: absorbances of standards, blanks and samples, titre volumes, weighed masses, or readings across a dilution series. Each sample is measured in repeats. Results that were already calculated can also be loaded as a table of value and unit.
data.item: one bench reading (a cuvette absorbance, a titration or a weighing) of one repeat of one sample

stage.text: calculating assay results from bench readings after the lab work, before writing up

mechanism.text: A sidebar switches between assay groups, a settings page, a page for already-calculated results and an overview. Each assay page runs in three numbered steps: what to measure, how to add readings, and the results. Readings uploaded or typed into the editable table are analysed straight away into summary metrics, a results table, colour-coded comparison flags, warnings and charts. The overview gathers every assay into one table and one Excel download.

field.text: colorimetric, titrimetric and gravimetric bench assays with standard curves in food chemistry

workflow.name: compute results from raw measurements by a fixed formula, check them, and report

steps.step: set the method parameters and comparison targets once
steps.here: Settings has a study tab (study name, SEM or SD, the CV limit for flagging repeats, the significance level) and a per-assay tab (calibration standard, equivalent label, wavelength, minimum R², titrant normality, IC50 method, and a reference sample or target range with its source). The settings are checked before saving

each assay page lists the columns it needs and offers a template to download. Readings come in as a CSV or XLSX upload or are typed into an editable table and sent with 'Analyze these readings'. A sidebar switch loads synthetic or supplied example data instead

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: it fits a linear standard curve after subtracting the blank, applies the titration or weighing formula, or fits IC50 three ways for a dilution series. It then gives mean ± SEM or SD per sample, with ANOVA/Tukey letters

steps.step: flag readings and samples that need attention
steps.here: it warns about a low standard-curve R², samples outside the standard range, repeats whose CV is above the limit (naming the repeat that deviates most), and readings below the detection limit, and counts the warnings in a metric

steps.step: compare each sample with a reference or a target range
steps.here: it compares sample means with a measured reference at the same dose or element, or with a target range in the same unit. Each sample gets a colour-coded flag (within target, below or above, no matching reference) and a suggested next step

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: the Overview page counts assays, samples and warnings, and shows one 'Results at a glance' table across all assays, with the comparison checks of each assay
it downloads an Excel workbook for one assay or for all of them. The workbook holds the calculation rows, the summaries, the warnings, the calibration and the settings used

distinctive: one registry of assays covers four kinds of calculation (standard curve, inhibition against a control, titration, gravimetric), and each assay group is a tab with the same three steps
readings below the detection limit are reported as ND, with the limit taken as 3 × SD of the blanks divided by the slope for each element, instead of as small invented numbers
a dilution series gives IC50 by logistic, interpolation and linear fits side by side, and IC50 is reported as a bound when 50% inhibition is never reached
a separate path accepts results that were already calculated and combines repeats only after the person confirms they are repeats, so no raw readings are invented
comparison flags are kept apart from significance tests, and a target range must carry the exact unit of the result and a recorded source

parts.title: Navigation and example-data switch
parts.summary: Moves between the overview, calculated results, each assay group and Settings, and switches between example data and the person's own readings.

parts.title: Settings
parts.summary: Holds the study-wide reporting choices and, for each assay, the calibration, titration or fitting parameters and the reference or target-range comparison, checking them before they are saved.

parts.title: Assay page
parts.summary: One tab per assay that explains the values to record and how to measure them, then takes readings and shows the results in three numbered steps.

parts.title: Add your readings
parts.summary: Offers a template for download, then takes a CSV or Excel upload or rows typed into an editable table, and lets the person clear an assay's readings.

parts.title: Understand your results
parts.summary: Shows counts of samples, warnings and flags, the results table with its unit, the warnings, standard-curve and dose-response charts, the full calculation tables and a download of the assay's report.
